answer: of 82 disagreeing faces that no literal opens, 6 are reached by a glob that names their own directory, 76 only by a glob that names an ancestor (so the sweep says nothing about which subdirectory), 0 only by a glob that names the file while '**' spans the directories, 0 only by sweeps with no naming segment at all, and 0 by no glob in the corpus (0 of the 82 absent from this checkout).
limits: the population is E606's publish: faces whose printed count disagrees with their own rows AND whose literal-reader count is zero. A face a literal opens but never reads a count from is E606's other class and is not here

a glob pattern is recovered from literals plus one-hop name assignments, os.path.join / Path composition and f-strings; a pattern built from a value this tracer cannot follow is published as a miss, not as a match

an argument this tracer cannot follow inside a composed pattern is filled with '*' -- that can only widen a pattern, never narrow it, so it can create an UNBOUNDED_ONLY reading but never a false NAMES_DIRECTORY one
matching is per segment (``*`` inside a segment, ``**`` across segments). fnmatch semantics would let '*' swallow separators and 'match' every face (E273/E470 family)
a glob that lands on a directory and is filtered by the caller afterwards counts as a landing: this measures reach, not consumption
faces missing from this checkout are published as face_absent rather than graded

E606 printed 81 faces with no reader at all; its own reader_pairs table holds 6 pairs across 5 faces, only 4 of which appear among the 86 face rows, so the row-level population here is 82. The one-face difference is E606's tally, disclosed rather than silently repaired
at most 8 sites per face are published; the counts are complete even when the site list is truncated
naming_rule: a path segment names something when literal text survives after its wildcards are stripped: '**' and '*' name nothing, 'FILEHIT*.json' names the file, 'results' names a directory
